 Los Angeles Lakers TST Best Bets: November 18, 2026
 By Nick Wire Nov 18, 2026 • 1:00 pm
 Share via facebook Share via X Share via email The Los Angeles Lakers continue their home stand tonight against the Utah Jazz. Last night, the Lakers came back from an 18 point deficit late in the third quarter and won in overtime against the Charlotte Hornets.
 The Lakers mixed a few different lineups while trying to fill in for starting center Walker Kessler, who missed the game with lower leg soreness. 
 Kessler is expected to return tonight, which should stabilize the lineup.
 With Kessler out, the Hornets blitzed Luka Dončić, forcing other players to step up. Guard Quentin Grimes took full advantage of the opportunity - dropping a career-high 47 points while hitting 10 threes in the process. 
 It was a barrage of threes from Grimes in the midst of the fourth quarter that helped the Lakers chip away at the Hornets' lead. Grimes nailed a game-tying three with a second to go in the fourth to send the game to overtime - where the Lakers' defense won the game from there.
 Dončić finished with 36 points on 13-for-34 shooting from the field. After the game, Dončić expressed frustration with his inefficient night and asserted that he must be better moving forward. 
 The Lakers' offense, outside of Dončić and without shooting guard Austin Reaves, must run through Grimes or backup point guard Collin Sexton - both of whom are flash in a pan scorers.

 First Pick: Luka Dončić over 35.5 points 
 Rundown:  Dončić had an off-night last night from the field - a brutal night - but he still had 36 points. The Last time Dončić played the Jazz, he dropped a season-high 52 points in Utah. Grimes' incredible shooting performance last night is not sustainable or reliable offense going forward, and Dončić, who was very frustrated with his poor shooting last night, will look to make up for his poor offensive output.
 Second Pick: Los Angeles Lakers over 119.5 points 
 Rundown: The Lakers average 122.5 points per game and they're playing a Jazz team that is 21st in defensive rating at 115.9. When the Lakers faced the Jazz a few weeks ago, they scored 132 points in the win. Yes, they'll likely be down Reaves in this game, but their paint stabilizer in Kessler is back - which opens up the pick and roll for Dončić and the Lakers' downhill wings like Sexton and Grimes.
